# Platform, tooling and guards: compliance register

What this is: the requirements of this area that are built and verified against running code, the typed rows recorded while building them, and coverage counts derived from the specs (verification.md §5). Requirements are in [`requirements.md`](../../requirements.md); deviations in [`deviations.md`](../deviations.md).

Row suffixes (requirements.md): -D defect in the sim, -B a choice the spec leaves open, -G declared gap, -V deviation from a "shall", -S spec contradiction and the reading chosen, -M mutant, -T T0 reading or measurement, -F a kaluza-core defect the sim found, -X retired. Verification: U unit, KAT or oracle test; F fuzz or property test; I interop; L lab; G gate row; A real-device comparison.

| KS-PLAT-B13 | 2026-10-14 | Runtime design (architecture §5) as built in M13. The timer wheel has four levels of 256 one-millisecond slots (2^32 ms) and an overflow list; advance() jumps to the next tick where a slot fires or a non-empty slot cascades, so hours of timers cost no idle ticks; a handle carries a generation and a fired or cancelled timer's node is released before its callback runs. The inbox is a bounded ring with per-cell sequence numbers (lock-free MPSC); post() fails when full, and only the post that finds no wake pending writes the eventfd. The shard runs at most a ring's worth of tasks per wake, so timers and descriptors are not starved, brings the wheel up to the clock before any task runs, and arms the timerfd for the wheel's next deadline only; its start_timer() counts a delay from the clock, not from the wheel's last advance, so a timer is never early (the M13 CI run under TSan caught a 30 ms timer firing 1 ms early through the wheel's own schedule_in). The log façade formats with fmt and cannot format SecretBytes (a static_assert); quill can replace its sink later | src/platform/timer_wheel.hpp, src/platform/mpsc.hpp, src/platform/shard.hpp, src/platform/log.hpp, M13 |

| KS-PLAT-B16 | 2026-10-15 | Runtime II as built in P1 N1 (ADR 0009 points 5 and 6). Executor (post, start_timer, stop_timer, now) is implemented by the real-time Shard and by SimLoop, a single-threaded virtual-time loop that runs posted tasks in order and otherwise jumps to the wheel's next deadline, firing by (deadline, scheduling order) as a Shard does; one conformance suite runs on both. Entities see only its TimerService half (R4). Rng is counter-based and keyed by (seed, key path): a stream's n-th value is SplitMix64's finaliser over key + n times the golden ratio, so streams never perturb each other and a run is a pure function of its seed (100 seeds, each run twice, alike; no two seeds alike). Yaml wraps yaml-cpp with strict scalars (only true/false; decimal or 0x integers with range checks), unknown-key refusal, and errors naming file:line:column and the path. EventRing numbers events in a bounded ring, long-polls with wait(), and calls its NDJSON listener under its lock so lines stay in seq order; event names are consteval literals that check_events.py ties to src/api/events.tsv. KSIM_MUTANT(name) is constant false unless built with KSIM_MUTATIONS=ON (preset mutants) and the process names the mutant in KSIM_MUTANT; check_mutants.py ties the sites to tests/mutants.tsv and its rows to gates/rows/p1.tsv. coro.hpp gives lazy Task<T>, spawn, CancelSource/CancelToken, sleep_for and a single-consumer Mailbox with a timeout; all resume inline on the actor's thread, so cancelling in an actor's destructor ends its procedures before its state goes (200 random cancel/expiry races: each waiter ends once, as expected, with no timer or frame left) | src/platform/{executor.hpp,sim_loop,rng,yaml,event,mutation,coro.hpp}; tests/unit/platform/{executor,sim_loop,rng,yaml,event,coro}_test.cpp; tools/guards/check_{events,mutants}.py; P1 N1 |

| KS-PLAT-B17 | 2026-10-15 | Transports as built in P1 N2 (ADR 0009; architecture §5). platform/transport.hpp defines the ports protocol code uses: IAssoc (SCTP-like: send with stream and PPID, up, negotiated stream counts, shutdown, abort; events up, restart, shutdown, lost, refused), IDatagram and IStream, plus Endpoint (numeric IPv4/IPv6, prefix membership). memlink implements IAssoc and IDatagram in memory between executors: one hop is delay_ms plus a seeded jitter, a direction never reorders, deliveries to a destroyed end are dropped. net implements them over kernel sockets: SCTP one-to-one sockets through <linux/sctp.h> only (no libsctp): SCTP_INITMSG, SCTP_NODELAY, SCTP_RECVRCVINFO, SCTP_EVENT for ASSOC_CHANGE and SHUTDOWN_EVENT, SCTP_SNDINFO/SCTP_RCVINFO cmsgs with the PPID in network order, SCTP_STATUS for the negotiated streams, partial delivery reassembled up to a bound, sends queued on EAGAIN, BINDX_ADD and CONNECTX for several addresses. A stream at or above the negotiated count is refused (L10). SctpClient re-associates after a loss or refusal with a doubling backoff (L11; TS 38.412 §7). UDP reads in recvmmsg batches of 64 and drops (counted) what the kernel will not take; TCP queues writes. One conformance suite runs on memlink in virtual time, memlink across two shards and SCTP over loopback (whole 100 KB messages, per-stream order, the stream bound, graceful shutdown, abort as lost), plus reconnect after a server restart and retry while refused; 30 repetitions clean, 10 under TSan. A handler may shut down or abort an association but must not destroy it | src/platform/{transport,memlink}; src/net/{sockaddr,sctp,udp,tcp}; tests/unit/net/{assoc,datagram}_test.cpp; P1 N2 |
